AC-2: the document specifies a capability-based PO boundary organized around four separated authorities named explicitly: OBSERVATION (read-only inspection -- already largely true today via READ_TOOLS' unrestricted file access, plus the new gh pr diff/gh run read-only commands and the evidence-reviewer agent this document scopes), GOVERNANCE AUTHORSHIP (writes confined to GOVERNANCE_PATHS, relay/*.json, and the new docs/design/po_drafts/*.md area, still never product source/tests/scripts), ENGINEERING EXECUTION (unchanged -- code, tests, state-file bookkeeping, merges, all remain the engineer's role), and HUMAN DECISION AUTHORITY (freeze, ratification, scope expansion, security/identity/credential/storage boundaries, real-device contact, waiver, deployment, and merge -- explicit human gates, listed as a closed set, not a PO capability under any standing delegation).

AC-3: the document specifies, precisely enough for GOV_PO_2_IMPLEMENTATION to build deterministically: (a) the exact new Bash prefixes to allowlist (gh pr diff, gh run view, gh run list -- read-only only, no gh run cancel/rerun/watch-with-side-effects) in both PO forms; (b) the docs/design/po_drafts/*.md pattern and the exact, deterministic status-line detection rule the gate must enforce to reject a PO-authored write containing a FROZEN or RATIFIED status marker (a concrete regex or field-based rule, not a vague 'detect intent' instruction); (c) that docs/history/INDEX.md is removed from the Edit/Write-reachable GOVERNANCE_PATHS list -- it becomes reachable only through scripts/build_history_index.py, already allowlisted, so this is a narrowing, not a new capability; (d) the exact mechanism for the offline repository-privacy-check capability -- this document must choose definitively between (i) a narrow, exact-match exception in the existing main.py token-denial check for precisely `<interpreter> main.py --repository-privacy-check` with no other arguments, or (ii) a new standalone equivalent checker script reusing utils/repository_privacy.py's logic without importing main.py's CLI surface -- state the choice and why, so GOV_PO_2_IMPLEMENTATION has zero open design questions on this point; (e) the new .claude/agents/nexus-po-evidence-reviewer.md agent's exact tool list and disallowed-tools list, modeled on the existing .claude/agents/nexus-council-seat.md pattern (Read/Grep/Glob only, Agent/Bash/Edit/Write explicitly disallowed, permissionMode: plan, no memory), plus the exact gate-side Agent-branch addition (subagent_type == 'nexus-po-evidence-reviewer', interactive form only, alongside the existing nexus-council-seat exception -- never a general allow-any-subagent_type widening).

AC-4: the document defines bounded standing-delegation classes -- routine review, correction, sequencing, backlog prioritization, movement slicing, and next-prompt production -- as named categories the Product Owner can authorize once, in writing, by class (mirroring GOV_PO_ROLE_MIGRATION.md D2's existing 'authorization persists within its stated scope until revoked or superseded' pattern), not as a new tool-enforced mechanism; a RELAY_DECISION's authorized_by field may cite a standing-delegation class by name as its source. Explicitly excluded from any standing-delegation class, restated as a closed list: freeze, ratification, scope expansion, security/identity/credential/storage-schema boundaries, real-device contact, waiver, deployment, and merge (of any kind, governance or product).

AC-5: the document states, as explicit policy (not a new gate mechanism -- restates and generalizes the practice already followed for gov_po_1_gate_4_issue_close_path and the M10.1/gate-3 backfill precedent), that project-state bookkeeping for a code-touching engineering movement is the engineer's own responsibility inside that movement's own commit/PR, not a separate PO-opened Lane-1 follow-up movement -- citing the gov_po_1_gate_3_agent_tool_council_path deferred-bookkeeping incident as the motivating precedent this rule closes.

AC-6: the document explicitly recommends that its own eventual freeze decision (a separate future DECIDE episode, not this PLAN) invoke nexus-decision-council under GOV_PO_ROLE_MIGRATION.md section 7 trigger (b) -- a freeze candidate introducing a write-boundary expansion for the PO role itself -- rather than freezing on the human's read alone; this movement does not invoke the council itself.

AC-7: this movement performs no other repository change -- no test, no gate code, no agent file, no roadmap logic beyond the bookkeeping GOV_PO_1's own contract already requires of every movement. It is, by design, the one document.

risks: The FROZEN/RATIFIED status-line detection rule is inherently a heuristic (a regex or field check over free-text Markdown) -- it can be evaded by a determined bad actor, but the PO assistant is not an adversarial actor in this trust model; the document must state this limitation honestly rather than claim a perfect guarantee, and note that the human's own review of any po_drafts/*.md file before treating it as authoritative remains the real control.

Choosing between a narrow main.py exception and a standalone privacy-check script is a real security-adjacent design call (does a narrow, well-tested exception in an already-hardened token-denial check introduce more risk than a new, smaller, purpose-built script reusing the same underlying utils.repository_privacy logic?) -- this document must give a reasoned recommendation, not defer the choice to the implementation movement.

This document proposes a real widening of what the PO role may do (new agent, new commands, new authoring area) -- even though every new capability stays read-only or DRAFT-only, it is the kind of change GOV_PO_ROLE_MIGRATION.md section 7 trigger (b) names for council review before freeze; AC-6 records that recommendation but does not act on it.
